reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) all concerns high-entropy alloy coatings on Q235 steel, not the base Q235 steel itself, and none addresses MnS inclusions, micro-galvanic coupling with inclusions, or the effect of inclusion removal on pitting. The key premises about MnS-driven pitting in Q235 are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Non-metallic inclusions (MnS) in Q235 steel act as micro-galvanic cells that initiate pitting
Reducing or altering surface inclusions will suppress localized corrosion
Electropolishing or local surface treatment can selectively remove/alter MnS inclusions
Pit initiation and corrosion rate are governed by inclusion density and distribution
The mechanism is generalizable to chloride environments at room and elevated temperatures
